source: Built-in five-study example, OR; unmodified counts
plain: This analysis combined 5 studies comparing event counts in two groups. The Mantel–Haenszel odds ratio was 0.299 (95% confidence interval 0.147 to 0.609). There is evidence of a difference (the confidence interval excludes no effect). The event may be beneficial or harmful; these numbers alone do not establish causation or clinical importance.
methods: Event counts and arm totals were pooled using a fixed-effect Mantel–Haenszel odds ratio with Robins–Breslow–Greenland variance. Peto one-step odds ratios were also computed as the exponential of summed observed-minus-expected events divided by summed hypergeometric variances; the log-scale standard error is the reciprocal square root of summed variances. Pooled estimates use the original counts without continuity correction. Double-zero-event studies contribute no information to pooled ratios; risk differences retain them. Pooled 95% confidence intervals use the estimate ± the standard-normal quantile times its standard error on the log scale, with exponentiation of estimates and limits. Two-sided normal z tests compare the analysis-scale estimate with zero, using the upper normal tail. No Hartung–Knapp adjustment is used. Per-study ratios and Wald intervals add 0.5 to every cell of a study if any cell is zero; other studies are uncorrected. No heterogeneity statistics, between-study variance, or prediction interval are computed for MH/Peto. The separately displayed fragility index uses greedy single-event modifications toward the null until a DerSimonian–Laird inverse-variance Wald interval includes zero on the analysis scale. This calculation drops studies with no events in both arms or all events in both arms, and corrects every cell of remaining zero-cell studies by 0.5. The fragility quotient divides the index by the total participants in all input studies. Non-significant starting results have no fragility index. The L’Abbé curve uses a separate inverse-variance fixed-effect risk ratio for the risk-ratio selection and odds ratio otherwise. Analyses were run in allmeta mh-peto <build.version> (commit <build.shortSha>).
results: There were 5 studies. MH OR = 0.299 (95% CI 0.147 to 0.609); z = −3.33; p = 0.001. Peto OR = 0.339 (95% CI 0.186 to 0.619); z = −3.53; p = 0.000. The separate DL fragility index was 7 event modifications (FQ = 0.0019).
flags: Displayed p values are rounded; a displayed zero does not imply a zero probability.
Peto estimates require caution with unbalanced arms or large effects.
Fewer than 10 studies: tests for small-study effects would be underpowered; none were performed.
